source_locators: Results and conclusions report 49.6 +/- 7.1 metres of glacier-front retreat immediately before the October 2023 event.
The reviewed full text identifies seven large calving events since 2017.
The authors interpret calving, moraine change, intermittent rainfall and breach as a combined event sequence rather than calving as a universal sole trigger.
Discussion and Figure 5 report more than 100 metres of retreat and approximately 7 million cubic metres of calved ice.
The reconstruction separately reports approximately 38.31 million cubic metres of landslide debris and combined displacement waves.
Landslide volume is retained as competing-event context and is not counted as calved-ice volume.
The official annex identifies the South Lhonak glacial-lake outburst as the primary reason for the sudden Teesta River surge while noting that the exact cause was still under investigation.
The report records 88,400 people affected across four districts and 100 villages or wards.
The report records 42 confirmed deaths in Sikkim, 77 missing people, 2,002 damaged houses and 33 damaged bridges as of 29 October 2023.

transformations.formula: Convert approximately 7,000,000 cubic metres of study-reported calved ice to 7 million cubic metres and normalize without adding the separately reported landslide-debris volume.
Normalize the official 88,400-person affected tally; retain deaths, missing people, houses and bridges as corroborating burden fields rather than summing unlike quantities.
Normalize seven large calving events documented since 2017; do not infer a global calving-frequency trend.
Normalize four officially affected Sikkim districts and retain 100 villages or wards as a separate boundary field.
0.35B + 0.30H + 0.20P + 0.15E; convert to 1-10 with 1 + 9 × composite and round to one decimal.

receipts.uncertainty: Front retreat and calved volume are study estimates with stated or study-specific remote-sensing uncertainty. The event reconstruction also identifies a much larger lateral-moraine landslide and displacement waves, and an independent trigger analysis emphasizes landslide processes; calving is therefore retained as one measured part of a compound event, not the sole cause. Official impacts are provisional as of 29 October 2023 and include the downstream GLOF disaster boundary, not impacts attributable exclusively to the calved-ice volume. No global frequency or global affected-area inference is made.
receipts.freshness: October 2023 event observations and official 29 October 2023 impact tally reviewed 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: Primary event reconstructions quantify front retreat, calved-ice volume and repeated calving, while the official disaster report quantifies the bounded downstream population and infrastructure burden.
higher_priority_failures: The evidence is a named glacier and disaster boundary, not a defensible global current aggregation.
The glacier-specific record does not provide at least 20 complete annual or 60 monthly global observations for historical-percentile normalization.
